prompt: When describing a data set, which features should you mention?
hint: A good description answers three questions about the data, not just one.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Use a sample of 3–4 values to see how the rule works, then apply it to the real data.
A good description answers three questions about the data, not just one.
Ask where the data is centered, how spread out it is, and what its overall shape looks like. Find the choice that covers all three.
The answer is A: mention the center, the spread and the shape.

explanation: The center, such as the mean or median, tells what a typical value is.
The spread, such as the range or IQR, tells how much the values vary.
The shape tells whether the data is symmetric or skewed and whether it has clusters, gaps or outliers.
A complete description uses all three, so the answer is choice A.
